artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: Appeal of TE Michael Chastain v. Heritage Presbytery. Chastain challenged Heritage Presbytery's judgment of guilty on charges of divisive behavior and censure of indefinite suspension from office and sacraments. The SJC sustained Presbytery's judgment, finding that Chastain's public letters to the congregation expressing disagreement with Session decisions violated his ordination vows to be subject to his brethren and maintain the peace and unity of the Church, even though his underlying views were not sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: TE James Thornton complained that Westminster Presbytery erred by declining to place a valid call from Memorial PCA into his hands and simultaneously invoking BCO 34-10 to begin divestiture proceedings. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the administrative remedy of BCO 34-10 cannot be invoked when a call is already in the presbytery's possession, and that presbytery's refusal lacked objective, justifiable grounds required for appellate review.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Anthony Dallison appealed his deposition from the office of Teaching Elder by North Florida Presbytery, arguing that presbytery lacked authority to increase his censure from indefinite suspension to deposition without conducting a new trial. The SJC affirmed presbytery's decision, holding that where a teaching elder has confessed guilt under BCO 38-1, presbytery may impose additional censure based on evidence of impenitence without initiating new charges, and such disciplinary discretion is within presbytery's constitutional authority.

artifacts.title: Morse v. Covenant Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission addressed three issues regarding actions of Covenant Presbytery involving TE Daniel R. Morse and Grace Presbyterian Church. The Commission ruled that teaching elders Morse and Crenshaw, having renounced communion with the PCA by joining the Reformed Episcopal Church, should be removed from presbytery rolls under BCO 38-3. The Commission found no provision requiring churches to notify presbytery before withdrawing from the PCA. Finally, the Commission determined that receiving and recording a protest is an administrative act, not a judicial decision, and that complaints regarding such actions are barred by BCO 45-5.

artifacts.title: Re-examination and divestiture of officers in rotational systems

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that the BCO provides no procedure for re-examining rotated-off officers' qualifications, but divestiture may only occur under BCO 24-6, 38-2, or 34-10.

artifacts.title: Session authority over officer nominees and inactive elders under rotation

matches.evidence: A session must present all qualified nominees for election and may not use BCO 24-6 to exclude inactive officers; presbytery proceedings are not automatically required for long-inactive elders.

artifacts.title: Teaching elder voting rights and congregational approval of pastoral salary changes

matches.evidence: The CCB advised that a teaching elder votes as a full session member, and that any change to pastoral salary terms requires congregational approval as part of the call.
